status_definitions.IMPLEMENTED: adapter code and offline tests exist
status_definitions.VALIDATED: 10-pair pilot passed (counts present, stable on repeat, guards held)
status_definitions.MEASURED: all 100 pairs measured in both languages
status_definitions.BLOCKED: not measured; reason recorded; no value published

measurement_methods.raw_content_tokens: locally reproduced encoding of the article text only: no special tokens, no chat template, no truncation; decode(encode(text)) == text verified per text
measurement_methods.api_input_tokens: input_tokens returned by the provider's official counting endpoint for one user message whose content is the article text; no system prompt, instructions or tools; includes provider framing, which is not removed

official_crosscheck.texts: all 200 corpus texts (100 Arabic, 100 English) plus 4 synthetic edge cases
official_crosscheck.reference: official implementations in an isolated environment: transformers 5.22.2 AutoTokenizer (DeepSeek, GLM: encode(add_special_tokens=False)); Kimi's own TikTokenTokenizer via trust_remote_code, encode(allow_special_tokens=False); tiktoken 0.14.0, tokenizers 0.23.3
official_crosscheck.result: token ids identical for every text and model (0 mismatches of 204 per model)
official_crosscheck.default_call_check: default encode('x') returns one token for all three: no BOS or chat markers added

deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017.source_note: Released tokenizer.json of this repository (byte-level BPE, 128,000 base tokens + 1,283 added; empty normalizer; ByteLevel post-processor adds no tokens). The official encoding/encoding.py renders messages as a string that this tokenizer encodes; message text is inserted verbatim. tokenizer_config.json: add_bos_token=false, add_eos_token=false. No older DeepSeek tokenizer is used.

glm-5.3-flash.source_note: Released tokenizer.json (byte-level BPE, 154,820 base tokens, ignore_merges=true; no normalizer; ByteLevel post-processor, no template). Chat markers such as [gMASK]<sop> and <|user|> come only from chat_template.jinja, which is not applied. Note: like the official encode, the runtime maps literal control strings in the text (e.g. [gMASK], <|user|>) to control ids even without add_special_tokens; ATTI refuses such content rather than counting it. None of the 200 corpus texts contains one.

kimi-k3.1-pro.source_note: tiktoken.model shipped in the K3.1 Pro repository itself (no other checkpoint's vocabulary is used). Pre-tokenization regex, the 400,000/25,000-character split rule and the 256 reserved special ids are reproduced from this revision's tokenization_kimi.py (SHA-256 204ee39fbf13a6d6608b0d3ca1b4b04a14ac5f0a062a7fdee02e61f5d936f9c6). encoding_k3.py encodes message text with allow_special=False, i.e. disallowed_special=(); counts here use the same call. Token-for-token identity with the official TikTokenTokenizer was checked on all 200 corpus texts.
